chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal from Ghalib ibn Uthman from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who prays the obligatory prayer, its time passes, he completes his prayer and recites the Tashahhud, then he sleeps before giving the Taslim. He said: 'His prayer is complete, and if he is one who suffers from istihadah (non-menstrual vaginal bleeding), he should wash it, then return and give the Taslim.'

key_terms.تَنْقَضِي صَلَاتُهُ: His prayer time expires / his prayer is completed
key_terms.رُعَافاً: One who suffers from istihadah (continuous minor impurity)
key_terms.غَسَلَهُ: He washed it (referring to the area of impurity or performing wudu)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one falls asleep after finishing the obligatory prayer but before saying Taslim?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the validity of the obligatory prayer is affirmed even if the worshipper falls asleep during the final sitting, highlighting the principle that the core pillars (arkan) have been fulfilled. The Imam provides a specific practical ruling for those with istihadah (continuous minor impurity), requiring them to wash the affected area and renew their state of purity before completing the prayer with the Taslim, thereby ensuring the ritual is concluded correctly despite the interruption.
